summary: Art-direct a compact family of highlight widths, roughness transitions and material-role contrasts while keeping glTF metallic-roughness transport explicit.
objective: Unlike assets share a recognizable light-response language, yet metal, dielectric, painted and emissive roles remain distinguishable under the target lighting.
applies_when: A stylized scene uses PBR materials rather than a fully unlit or toon-only pipeline.
Materials match by swatch in Blender but drift under runtime lighting.
intent_signals: consistent highlight widths across props and architecture
example_prompts: Give an enamel kettle and a stone arch a shared broad-highlight language while preserving metal, coating and stone roles after glTF export.
negative_signals: Using base color alone to label every material.
Assuming a Blender viewport node network is the interchange contract.

principles: Define response roles before values: broad quiet body, narrow focal glint, broken granular response, and optional emissive accent. Map each asset material to a role, then tune within it.
Use stylization to compress or exaggerate response differences deliberately. Keep metal/dielectric identity and transport assumptions inspectable rather than treating every bright highlight as paint.
Judge the response under the target key, fill and environment plus one stress rotation; a pleasing front view alone is insufficient.
implementation: In Blender, author a response swatch board beside two unlike assets. Keep base color, metallic, roughness, normal frequency and emissive intent separable; bake unsupported procedural marks to declared textures.

Export glTF metallic-roughness data and inventory material slots. The core texture stores roughness in green and metalness in blue with linear encoding; custom ramps, layered node logic and compositor treatment need baking, extensions or a Three.js rebuild.

In Three.js, load the transported PBR values first, then add optional response quantization, rim or outline as a documented runtime layer. Retest under the actual environment map and tone mapping; do not silently compensate by rewriting all source values.
observable_checks: A rotating light or object produces the declared broad, narrow and broken response roles on both unlike assets without collapsing them into the same material.
Inspect exported channels and runtime material values: a roughness/metalness swap or color-space mistake is visible in the swatch board before scene review.
Disable custom runtime shading: the base glTF materials remain interpretable and the missing stylized layer is explicitly recorded rather than mistaken for export loss.

creative_affordances: Use a two-band roughness family, oversized soft glints or sparse high-frequency breakup according to the brief.
Reserve one response exception for the focal or interactive material.
known_limits: glTF metallic-roughness transport does not reproduce arbitrary Blender shader graphs or guarantee identical lighting and tone mapping.
The response roles and swatch choices are authored guidance, not measured material truth. No runtime comparison was run.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 metallic-roughness materials sample roughness from the green channel and metalness from the blue channel of the metallic-roughness texture, require linear encoding for those values, and ignore red and alpha for these calculations.
claims.scope: Khronos glTF 2.0.1 core metallic-roughness material; extensions and renderer-specific stylization remain separate.
